# The command line

```
usage: drawspec [-h] [--version]
                {render,validate,theme,schema,kinds,example,mcp} ...
```

Nothing is printed to stdout but the thing that was asked for — the SVG, the
schema, or a one-line confirmation — so `drawspec render doc.json > doc.svg`
is safe. Refusals go to stderr **in full**: the message names the remedy as
well as the fault, and a build script that truncates it to a summary line is a
build script whose author ends up guessing.

## Exit codes

The split is worth stating: **2 is about the invocation, 1 is about the
content.** A misspelt flag or an unknown profile is 2 — nothing was read, so
nothing can be said about it. A document that cannot be read, cannot be parsed,
or cannot be fitted is 1, and a refusal is an outcome, not a crash.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | It worked. |
| `1` | The document, the theme or the fit was refused. |
| `2` | The command line itself was wrong. |

## Global options

Legal before the command name.

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--version` | Show program's version number and exit. |

## Commands

### `drawspec render`

Read a document, draw it, and write the SVG to stdout or to a file. With --format png, or an -o ending in .png, write a PNG instead (needs pip install 'drawspec[png]'). With --format text, or an -o ending in .txt, write the diagram as plain text, refused when it is wider than --width.

```
usage: drawspec render [-h] [-o OUT] [--theme THEME] [--variant NAME=THEME]
                       [--width WIDTH] [--height HEIGHT]
                       [--profile {inline,standalone}]
                       [--format {svg,png,text}] [--charset {unicode,ascii}]
                       [--scale SCALE] [--background {light,dark,transparent}]
                       document
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `document` | The document to render. |
| `-o`, `--out` | Write here instead of stdout. |
| `--theme` | A bundled theme name or a theme file. |
| `--variant` | For svg: also draw the diagram in THEME, switched on by an ancestor's data-theme=NAME (and, for NAME dark, by prefers-color-scheme). Repeatable. --theme is the base and answers to light. |
| `--width` | Override the document's width; with --format text, the most terminal cells a line may take (default 80, or 100 for lanes, sequence and timing). |
| `--height` | Override the document's height. |
| `--profile` | The embedding profile. One of `inline`, `standalone`. Default `inline`. |
| `--format` | What to write: svg; png, a raster image of the standalone drawing; or text, the diagram as plain text for a code block or a terminal (files, tree, sequence, gantt, timeline, board, stack, rag, meter, network, timing, gitgraph, flow, states, lanes). Default: from the -o extension, else svg. One of `svg`, `png`, `text`. |
| `--charset` | For text: box-drawing characters, or ASCII only (default unicode). One of `unicode`, `ascii`. |
| `--scale` | For png: pixels per SVG unit, at most 8 (default 2). |
| `--background` | For png: theme ink on white, light ink on near-black, or no page (default light). One of `light`, `dark`, `transparent`. |

### `drawspec validate`

Parse and check a document, drawing nothing. Every violation is printed with the JSON pointer of the place it was written.

```
usage: drawspec validate [-h] [--theme THEME] document
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `document` | The document to validate. |
| `--theme` | A bundled theme name or a theme file. |

### `drawspec theme`

Tools for the files that decide appearance.

```
usage: drawspec theme [-h] {check,from} ...
```

#### `drawspec theme check`

Load a theme and run its invariants, the greyscale role pairing included.

```
usage: drawspec theme check [-h] theme
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `theme` | A bundled theme name or a theme file. |

#### `drawspec theme from`

Read CSS custom properties (a .css file) or W3C design tokens (a .json or .tokens file) and write the theme they map onto, as TOML. Fonts, the accent and muted colours, a corner radius and a stroke weight are taken; every token left out is reported on stderr with the reason. A colour that would not read at 3:1 on both a white and a near-black page is darkened or lightened until it does. Local files only: no URL is fetched.

```
usage: drawspec theme from [-h] [-o OUT] [--name NAME] [--strict]
                           brand [brand ...]
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `brand` | A .css or design-tokens file; a later file wins a tie. |
| `-o`, `--out` | Write here instead of stdout. |
| `--name` | The theme's name; the first file's name by default. |
| `--strict` | Refuse a colour that would need adjusting, instead of adjusting it. |

### `drawspec schema`

Write the published document JSON Schema, for editor completion.

```
usage: drawspec schema [-h] [--out OUT]
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--out` | Write here instead of stdout. |

### `drawspec kinds`

One line per kind: the claim that kind of diagram makes.

```
usage: drawspec kinds [-h]
```

### `drawspec example`

Write the smallest document of that kind that renders, to stdout. Pipe it straight back in: drawspec example flow | drawspec validate -

```
usage: drawspec example [-h]
                        {flow,tree,cycle,stack,timeline,columns,matrix,pyramid,rings,funnel,chart,quadrant,scatter,curve,files,states,sequence,lanes,entities,gantt,board,fishbone,venn,journey,treemap,sankey,numberline,barmodel,waterfall,pie,mindmap,argument,familytree,meter,rag,clock,sunburst,network,timing,gitgraph}
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `kind` | Which kind to write. One of `flow`, `tree`, `cycle`, `stack`, `timeline`, `columns`, `matrix`, `pyramid`, `rings`, `funnel`, `chart`, `quadrant`, `scatter`, `curve`, `files`, `states`, `sequence`, `lanes`, `entities`, `gantt`, `board`, `fishbone`, `venn`, `journey`, `treemap`, `sankey`, `numberline`, `barmodel`, `waterfall`, `pie`, `mindmap`, `argument`, `familytree`, `meter`, `rag`, `clock`, `sunburst`, `network`, `timing`, `gitgraph`. |

### `drawspec mcp`

The MCP server; needs the extra: pip install 'drawspec[mcp]'.

```
usage: drawspec mcp [-h]
```

## Embedding profiles

`render --profile` takes `inline`, `standalone`.

* **`inline`** — for pasting into a Markdown or HTML page. Strokes are
  `currentColor`, so the drawing inherits the page's ink and follows it into
  dark mode; there is no `<style>` block to leak, and every id is scoped so two
  diagrams on one page cannot collide.
* **`standalone`** — for a linked `.svg`, a PDF conversion, or anywhere there
  is nothing to inherit from. `currentColor` is resolved to the theme's
  `[canvas] ink`, because a converter's own default is not a design decision.

## Themes

`--theme` takes a bundled theme name or the path of a TOML file. See
[the theme reference](theme.md) for every key a theme may set, and
[the guide](guide.md) for how to write one.
